Counsel for Respondent :- Vashishtha Tiwari Hon'ble Vipin Chandra Dixit,J.

1 . Heard Sri Dinkar Mani Tripathi, learned counsel for the appellant and Sri Vashishtha Tiwari,
learned counsel for the claimant-respondent nos.1 & 2.
2.

This first appeal from order has been filed on behalf of claimant-appellant under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 against the judgement and award dated 30.10.2009 passed by Additional District Judge, Court No. 8/Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Deoria, in M.A.C.P. No.
208 of 2008, by which, compensation of Rs.3,14,000/- along with 6% interest has been awarded on account of death of Aditya Kumar Baranwal aged about 18 years, who died in a road accident on 06.04.2008.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant submits that it was a case of head-on collision in between bus of appellant corporation and motorcycle bearing No. KA 04 EN/4201.
The accident was occurred on account of sole negligence of motorcyclist and there was no negligence on the part of driver of appellant corporation.
It is further submitted that the Claims Tribunal has erred in deciding issue no.1 holding the rash and negligent driving of bus driver.
The compensation awarded to the claimants is also on higher side.
4. No other ground has been pressed by learned counsel for the appellant.
5. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondents submits that the accident was occurred on account of rash and negligent driving of bus driver.
The claimant had produced one Santosh Kumar Baranwal, who was an eye witness of the accident, who fully proved the rash and negligent driving of driver of bus of appellant corporation.
The F.I.R. was lodged against the driver of the appellant corporation and Investigating Officer after due investigation has also submitted charge sheet against the driver of bus.

The driver of bus produced by the appellant corporation as D.W.-1 was an interested witness as the chargesheet was submitted against him and that claims tribunal has rightly disbelieved the evidence of driver of bus.
The finding recorded by claims tribunal in respect of rash and negligent driving of bus driver is based on evidence and material which are available on record.

It is further submitted that compensation awarded by the Claims Tribunal is almost just and proper and cannot said to be excessive in any manner.
6.
Considered the submissions of learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
7. The claimants had produced Santosh Kumar Baranwal as P.W.-2, who was an eye witness of the accident who has stated that the bus was driven by its driver very rashly and negligently.
The first information report was lodged against bus driver.
The Investigating Officer had also submitted charge sheet against the bus driver.
No authentic evidence has been adduced by the appellant corporation to prove the rash and negligent driving of motorcyclist.

Even otherwise the deceased was pillion rider on motorcycle and, as such, in any view of the matter, it was a case of composite negligence and there was no contribution on the part of the deceased in the accident.
The findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal in respect of negligence of bus driver is based on evidence and there is no illegality in any manner.
8. The compensation of Rs.3,14,000/- awarded for the death of young boy aged about 18 years cannot said to be excessive in any manner.
No ground for interference is made out.
9. The appeal is devoid of merits and is, accordingly, dismissed.
10. Interim order, if any, stands discharged.
